chunks: My father (rah) said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Ibn Abi Najran, who raised it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
One who patches his garment, stitches his shoe, and carries his own merchandise has freed himself from pride.
ai.seo_question: How does carrying one's own luggage help a Muslim overcome pride?
ai.summary: In *Thawab al-A'mal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), linking the physical acts of mending garments and carrying one's own load to the eradication of *kibr* (arrogance), a trait often associated with the elite's detachment from manual labor. This teaching emphasizes that humility is cultivated not just through spiritual introspection but through tangible, everyday engagement in one's own affairs, serving as a practical antidote to the ego's pride.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. My father (rah) said: it was narrated to me by Ahmad b. Idris from Muhammad b. Ahmad from Ya’qub b. Yazid from Ibn Abi Najran who raised it to Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said: “
One who patches his clothes, stitches his shoes and carries his own luggage will remain away from pride.”
